messages:
maya: FYI customer AcmeCorp hit 403s on SSO after their IdP cert rotation. They say this started ~09:10 UTC. Error in our logs: 'InvalidRecipient' and also a note 'token-binding mismatch'.

sam: Can you paste the assertion recipient and the raw error log? Does the SAMLResponse show the exact ACS URL?

maya: Pasting redacted excerpts from the support logs (base64 decoded assertion):
```
SubjectConfirmationData Recipient="https://app.acme.com:443/saml/acs" NotOnOrAfter="2026-03-17T09:10:12Z"
Assertion Issuer="https://idp.customer.example/metadata"
SignedInfo Reference URI="#_abc123"
Signature Thumbprint="SHA256:AA:BB:CC:..:FF"
```
Server error snippet:
```
2026-03-17T09:10:12Z auth[sso]: validation failed: recipient mismatch (expected https://app.acme.com/saml/acs) -> 403 InvalidRecipient
also: binding mismatch: expected urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:cm:bearer got urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:cm:holder-of-key
```

eli: Two things jumping out: IdP included explicit :443 in SubjectConfirmationData and our RP recipient canonicalization strips default HTTPS port. That causes the recipient check to fail. Second, the binding type changed to holder-of-key — likely tied to new key usage after rotation.

eli: Short repro I used locally: POST the SAMLResponse to /sso/_debug/acs with curl -> we return 403 with same 'InvalidRecipient'. Example (redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST https://auth.redwood.test/sso/_debug/acs -d 'SAMLResponse=<base64>' -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" -v
```

maya: Customer says their IdP operator rotated and then re-published metadata with a slightly different entity descriptor that includes port in the ACS location. They also rotated signing key. They're willing to republish without the port if we confirm that's the issue.

idp-admin: Sorry about the churn — rotation process added the port to the exported metadata. We can publish a cleaned metadata (remove :443) now. Also we changed the default assertion signing method which ended up issuing holder-of-key assertions because the new key was labeled as 'keyAgreement'. We'll republish fixed metadata in 20m.

sam: Ops action items: 1) Temporarily accept ACS URLs that match host+path ignoring default port to avoid customer downtime (config flag accept_acs_with_default_port=true). 2) Add a short-lived matching fallback for 'holder-of-key' -> treat as bearer when no keyInfo present (safe for a week while IdP migrates). 3) Notify eng-sre to validate cert propagation across our edge caches (I saw old certs cached in some regions).

eli: Config snippet to flip locally for testing (do not commit to main without workaround gate):
```yaml
saml:
  receiver:
    accept_acs_with_default_port: true
    fallback_bindings:
      - holder-of-key-as-bearer: true # temporary
```

sso-bot: incident created -> #inc-2026-117 assigned to eng-sre (priority: P2) :rotating_light:

maya: I'll coordinate with AcmeCorp support contact, will ask them to re-publish metadata now and I will confirm once their new metadata hits our fetcher. Also will schedule a quick canary of the fallback config in staging. :thumbsup:

sam: Follow-ups: verify metadata fetch TTL (currently 300s) — recommend reduce to 60s for faster convergence for this migration window. Check logs for other tenants that might have published with explicit default ports.

eli: I'll prepare a short rollback checklist for the temporary flags and a post-mortem note template.

maya: Thanks — keeping customer updated, will post status here when metadata is live and when staging canary runs.
